source_meta._title: Certain entity animations stop after they've existed in world for too long

stor.environment: Unmodified vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition 1.16.2 in a new single-player Creative-mode world. The test uses one bee in a transparent enclosure near the player so that the entity remains loaded throughout the required continuous waiting period. No multiplayer server, special seed, resource pack, or mod is required.
preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher to start the exact affected version 1.16.2, which is the first version listed in the report.
Use an unmodified vanilla installation; disable Forge, Fabric, OptiFine, and other client or server mods for this reproduction.
Allow at least 82 minutes of uninterrupted in-world test time after the bee is spawned.
The single-player world must remain actively running during the wait. Do not open the Esc pause menu, return to the title screen, close the game, or allow the game to pause when it loses focus.
Keep the bee's chunk loaded for the entire wait by remaining near the bee. Do not teleport away, change dimensions, kill the bee, or replace it with another bee.
Creative mode is selected as a practical setup method so commands can create a controlled enclosure and spawn the bee deterministically.

steps.action: Start Minecraft: Java Edition using the 1.16.2 installation. On the title screen, confirm that the displayed version is exactly 1.16.2 before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and identifies the running version as 1.16.2.

steps.action: Create a disposable single-player Creative-mode world. From the title screen, select Singleplayer, select Create New World, change Game Mode to Creative, and select Create New World. No particular seed or world-generation option is required.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: A new world begins loading with the player configured for Creative mode.

steps.action: Wait for world generation and chunk loading to finish. Do not begin the timed portion while the loading screen is visible or while nearby terrain is still appearing. Confirm that normal movement and camera controls respond.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the world, nearby terrain is rendered, movement responds normally, and the Creative-mode inventory is available.

steps.action: Without moving during command entry, create a transparent 7-by-7-by-7 glass enclosure centered around the player. Press T to open in-game chat, type the command exactly with its leading slash, and press Enter. The hollow enclosure supplies a glass floor, walls, and roof while leaving enough interior air for the bee to move.
steps.success_cue: A closed transparent glass enclosure surrounds the player, with an approximately 5-by-5-by-5-block air space inside and no opening through which the bee can escape.

steps.action: Spawn one bee inside the enclosure. Press T to open in-game chat, type the command exactly with its leading slash, and press Enter. Do not attack or otherwise replace the bee after it is summoned.
steps.success_cue: Exactly one live bee is visible inside the glass enclosure near the player, and the chat command reports a successful summon.

steps.action: Treat completion of the summon command as the beginning of the bee's existence time and immediately start an external elapsed-time timer. Leave the player inside the enclosure and within several blocks of the bee.
steps.exact_input: Start timer at 00:00 immediately after the successful summon
steps.success_cue: The elapsed-time timer is running, the bee remains nearby, and both the player and bee are inside the same enclosure.

steps.action: Keep the world continuously active while the timer runs. Stay inside or immediately beside the enclosure so the bee's chunk remains loaded. Keep Minecraft focused, do not open the Esc pause menu, do not leave the world, do not change dimensions, and do not execute any command that kills, reloads, or replaces the bee. It is acceptable to adjust the camera without interacting with the bee.
steps.success_cue: The world remains unpaused and responsive, the original bee is still alive inside the enclosure, and the elapsed-time timer continues increasing.

steps.action: Continue the uninterrupted wait until at least 82 minutes have elapsed since the bee was summoned. This exceeds the report's approximately 98,000-to-98,200-tick bee threshold at the normal rate of 20 game ticks per second. As the timer reaches 82 minutes, keep the original bee rendered nearby and aim the camera so its body and wings are clearly visible, without evaluating the animation yourself.
steps.exact_input: Wait until elapsed time is at least 01:22:00
steps.success_cue: At least 82 minutes of continuous, unpaused in-world time have elapsed since the summon; the original bee is still loaded, alive, nearby, and clearly framed for visual inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: At least 82 minutes of continuous active world time have elapsed since the original bee was summoned, and that bee remains loaded and clearly visible inside the glass enclosure. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately without pausing, reloading, leaving the world, or spawning a replacement bee.
uncertainties: The original reproduction text says to wait about 81 minutes, while the report's detailed analysis places the bee threshold at approximately 98,040 to 98,200 ticks, or roughly 81 minutes 42 seconds to 81 minutes 50 seconds at 20 ticks per second. The plan therefore uses at least 82 minutes.

Wall-clock time assumes the world sustains approximately 20 ticks per second. If the game runs below 20 ticks per second, more than 82 minutes of wall-clock time may be required to accumulate the reported entity age.

The report also describes an optional bat reproduction at approximately 158,400 to 158,600 ticks, about 132 minutes. That branch is omitted because the report explicitly makes the bat optional and the bee provides the shorter deterministic reproduction.
The glass enclosure and commands are practical setup choices rather than requirements stated by the report. They are used to prevent the bee from leaving the loaded area during the long wait.

source_meta._title: Leashes from two or more invisible entities connect to each other

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 21w03a running an unmodified vanilla client. Use a single-player world on the integrated server, Creative mode, cheats enabled, a first-person non-Spectator viewpoint, and no active third-party resource packs or shader modifications. A new Superflat world is recommended as a practical way to provide an unobstructed test area, but Superflat is not a report requirement.
preconditions: Install and select the exact Java Edition snapshot 21w03a in the Minecraft Launcher; do not use the fix version 22w15a.
Disable non-default resource packs, shader replacements, and client mods, because a comment reports that a patched leash shader can conceal the rendering issue.

Use a keyboard and mouse with the normal action mappings or their rebound equivalents: T for chat, E for inventory, right-click for Use Item/Place Block, and number keys or the mouse wheel for hotbar selection.
Ensure the test world permits commands. The recommended setup is a new Creative-mode single-player world with Allow Cheats enabled.
Perform the test in Creative mode or another normal player mode, not Spectator mode; a report comment states that the relevant rendering is not visible while viewing in Spectator mode.
Use an open location where both summoned cows and their leash paths can be viewed without blocks obscuring them.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the installation profile for snapshot 21w03a. At the title screen, confirm that the displayed version is 21w03a before opening a world.
steps.success_cue: The 21w03a title screen is loaded and the version label identifies the running game as 21w03a.

steps.action: Create a single-player test world. Select Creative as the game mode, open More World Options, ensure Allow Cheats is ON, and optionally select Superflat to obtain an unobstructed area. Create the world and wait until terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a fully loaded world in Creative mode and commands are permitted.

steps.action: Move to an open, level area. To make the report's relative summon coordinates place the cows directly in front of the camera, open the F3 debug screen and rotate until the Facing line says north, toward negative Z; then close the debug screen. Stand still at this position while executing both summon commands.
steps.exact_input: F3; rotate until facing north (toward negative Z); F3
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary in an unobstructed area and is facing toward negative Z, with room approximately three blocks ahead and one block to each side.

steps.action: Open in-game chat, enter the report's first summon command exactly with the leading slash, and submit it. Execute the command from in-game chat rather than a server console.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds and a cow is visible approximately one block to the player's right and 2.5 blocks ahead. It remains stationary because NoAI is enabled.

steps.action: Without changing the player's position, open chat again, enter the report's second summon command exactly with the leading slash, and submit it.
steps.success_cue: A second stationary cow appears approximately one block to the player's left and 2.5 blocks ahead; exactly two newly summoned cows are positioned side by side in front of the player.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory with E. Select the Search Items tab, search for Lead, and place a stack containing at least two leads into one of the nine hotbar slots along the bottom of the inventory. Close the inventory with E.
steps.exact_input: E; search for "Lead"; move leads to a hotbar slot; E
steps.success_cue: At least two leads are available in one of the player's nine hotbar slots and the world view is open again.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the leads by pressing its corresponding number key from 1 through 9 or by scrolling the mouse wheel until that slot is highlighted.
steps.exact_input: Corresponding hotbar number key, or mouse wheel
steps.success_cue: The lead slot has the hotbar selection outline and a lead is shown as the held item.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair directly at the first cow and use the held lead on it with right-click. Do not right-click a fence, because the selected reproduction keeps the leads attached to the player.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the first cow while holding a lead
steps.success_cue: A normal leash line runs from the first cow to the player, confirming that the first cow is leashed.

steps.action: Keep the leads selected, aim directly at the second cow, and right-click it once to attach another lead.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the second cow while holding a lead
steps.success_cue: Both visible cows are independently leashed to the player, with one normal leash line leading from each cow to the player.

steps.action: Return to or remain near the original position between the two cows. Face both cows so that the cows and both complete leash paths are simultaneously inside the camera view. Do not enter Spectator mode.
steps.success_cue: Both cows and both player-to-cow leash lines are visible together in the same first-person view.

steps.action: While both cows remain leashed to the player, open in-game chat and execute the report's invisibility command exactly with the leading slash. Do not move far enough to break either lead while entering the command.
steps.success_cue: The command reports successful application to the two nearest cows, both cow bodies become invisible, and both leads remain attached to the player and to the cows' fixed locations.

steps.action: After chat closes, aim at the area containing both invisible cows and their leash endpoints. Keep both leash paths in frame. If necessary, make small camera rotations or take a small step without exceeding lead range so the full rendered geometry of both leads is unobstructed; do not continue until both leash paths can be inspected together.
steps.exact_input: Move mouse slowly to adjust the camera; optionally tap a movement key for a small viewpoint adjustment
steps.success_cue: The player remains in a non-Spectator mode, both invisible cows are still leashed to the player, and the complete visible leash geometry for both entities is framed for immediate inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: Both stationary cows have just received the invisibility effect while independently leashed to the player, and the non-Spectator camera is positioned so both leash paths and both invisible-cow endpoint locations can be inspected together. Hand control to the observation subsystem now.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, world type, game difficulty, or single-player versus dedicated-server environment. A new single-player Creative world with cheats is selected as the simplest deterministic execution environment.
Creative mode and the Creative inventory are practical choices for obtaining the leads; the report requires two leads but does not require a particular acquisition method or game mode.

The description mentions placing the cows in glass boxes, but the formal Steps to Reproduce instead summon them with NoAI:1b. Glass boxes are omitted because the supplied commands already keep the cows stationary.

The report does not specify an exact viewing angle. A comment notes that the result can be hidden from certain angles, so the plan frames both leash paths and permits small camera adjustments without defining the rendering outcome to look for.
The reproduction uses leads attached to the player. The description says the condition can also occur with leads tied to a fence, but the formal steps do not require a fence.

The command selector has no distance restriction. The two summoned cows should be the nearest cows because they are placed approximately 2.7 blocks from the player; using a new open test world further reduces the possibility of selecting unrelated cows.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-264821:The fog on armor worn by entities occurs too early
source_meta._title: Fog on moving pistons happens too early

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.18.1 Pre-release 1, using a single-player integrated server, a fresh Superflat Overworld, Creative mode with cheats enabled, the default resource pack, no shaders or rendering mods, and Render Distance set to 2 chunks.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher can install and launch the historical Java Edition version listed as 1.18.1 Pre-release 1.
Use an unmodified client. Disable shaders, rendering mods, and non-default resource packs so they do not change fog or piston rendering.
A keyboard and mouse are available. Instructions name default controls; use the corresponding bound control if keys have been remapped.
The test world is disposable because the procedure places blocks at fixed coordinates near X=0, Z=0.
Commands must be permitted in the world.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for the report's first affected version, 1.18.1 Pre-release 1, and launch it. This version is also identified as 1.18.1-pre1. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/Java%E7%89%881.18.1-pre1?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The title screen is open and identifies the running version as 1.18.1 Pre-release 1 or 1.18.1-pre1.

steps.action: From the title screen, open the single-player world creation screen.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open.

steps.action: Set Game Mode to Creative. Open More World Options and ensure Allow Cheats is ON so the setup commands can be executed.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; More World Options... -> Allow Cheats: ON
steps.success_cue: The creation screen shows Creative mode and cheats enabled.

steps.action: While in More World Options, cycle World Type until Superflat is selected. Leave the seed and Superflat preset at their defaults, then return to the main creation screen.
steps.success_cue: The world creation screen shows the Superflat world type.

steps.action: Create the world and wait without entering commands until world loading finishes and normal player movement is responsive.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a Superflat Overworld and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Set the client to the low render distance recommended by the report. Press Esc, open Options, open Video Settings, set Render Distance to 2 chunks, and select Done until gameplay resumes. Two chunks is a valid render-distance value for this version family. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/%E5%AE%A2%E6%88%B7%E7%AB%AF%E9%80%89%E9%A1%B9%E6%96%87%E4%BB%B6%E6%A0%BC%E5%BC%8F?variant=zh-tw&utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options... -> Video Settings... -> Render Distance: 2 chunks -> Done -> Done
steps.success_cue: Gameplay has resumed with Render Distance displayed as 2 chunks in Video Settings.

steps.action: Enter Creative flight so the player will remain suspended while the elevated test platform is constructed. Rapidly press the jump control twice; the default key is Space.
steps.success_cue: The player can hover and does not fall when movement keys are released.

steps.action: Open chat with T, enter the teleport command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter. This moves the player near the fixed construction area while preserving flight.
steps.success_cue: The player is hovering near X=0, Y=105, Z=-8 and has not fallen toward the Superflat ground.

steps.action: Wait until the surrounding chunk has loaded and commands and movement respond normally before placing the test structure.
steps.success_cue: No loading screen is present, the sky and distant Superflat terrain render normally, and player movement is responsive.

steps.action: Standardize illumination by opening chat, executing the command, and pressing Enter.
steps.success_cue: The world is in daytime with bright overhead illumination.

steps.action: Remove weather as a visual obstruction by opening chat, executing the command, and pressing Enter.
steps.success_cue: There is no rain, snow, or thunder at the test location.

steps.action: Create an 11-by-11 static stone comparison platform. Open chat, enter the command exactly as shown, and press Enter. Java Edition setblock/fill block arguments support namespaced block identifiers and block-state syntax in this command format. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/%E5%91%BD%E4%BB%A4/setblock?variant=zh-cn&utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: A square stone platform is visible below the player, centered near X=0, Y=99, Z=0.

steps.action: Place the test piston in the center of the platform, facing upward. Open chat, enter the command exactly as shown, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: An upward-facing piston is present at the center of the stone platform.

steps.action: Place the outer half of the two-observer redstone clock. Open chat, enter the command exactly as shown, and press Enter. The selected observer facing value makes its redstone output point east and its detecting face point west. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Module%3ASchematic/titles?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: An observer is present two blocks east of the piston; the piston is not required to cycle yet.

steps.action: Complete and start the redstone clock by placing the second observer between the piston and the first observer. Open chat, enter the command exactly as shown, and press Enter. Its output points west toward the piston, while the two observers' detecting faces point toward one another. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Module%3ASchematic/titles?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The upward-facing piston repeatedly extends and retracts without further player input.

steps.action: Remain near the platform briefly and confirm that the redstone clock continues running rather than producing only one piston movement. Do not proceed during a chunk-loading pause.
steps.success_cue: At least three complete piston extension-and-retraction cycles have occurred and player movement remains responsive.

steps.action: Move to a repeatable distant viewing position. Open chat, enter the teleport command exactly as shown including the final yaw and pitch values, and press Enter. This places the player north of and above the platform, facing south and downward toward it.
steps.success_cue: The stone platform is approximately centered in view below and ahead of the player, and the piston remains inside the rendered scene.

steps.action: Do not evaluate the bug yet. Wait until the platform and piston have rendered fully, the piston is visibly continuing its mechanical cycle, and movement and commands respond without chunk-loading delay.
steps.success_cue: The platform is loaded, the player is stationary, and the piston continues extending and retracting at the center of the platform.

steps.action: Fine-tune the viewing distance to satisfy the report's fog-boundary condition. Keep looking at the piston and use short taps of the flight-up control (default Space), flight-down control (default Left Shift), forward control (default W), or backward control (default S). Remain approximately within X=0, Y=116 to 126, and Z=-22 to -28. Stop moving as soon as the surrounding static stone platform is close to the fog boundary but is still identifiable, while the piston continues cycling.
steps.exact_input: Short taps of Space, Left Shift, W, or S as needed
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary near the fog boundary; the surrounding stone platform remains discernible, the piston location is centered or nearly centered, and the piston continues cycling.

stor.handoff_condition: The player is stationary at a low-render-distance vantage near the fog boundary, looking toward the continuously cycling upward-facing piston and its surrounding static stone platform. Chunk loading is complete and controls are responsive; begin rendering observation now.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, game mode, world type, graphics quality, clock design, or exact render-distance value. The fresh Superflat Creative world, fixed coordinates, two-observer clock, and 2-chunk render distance are practical deterministic setup choices.

The report refers to pistons in the plural but does not prescribe a minimum count. This plan uses one repeatedly moving piston to minimize setup complexity while preserving the stated piston-clock interaction.

The exact point described as close to being obscured by fog can vary with camera position and client presentation. Step 17 provides a repeatable starting position, and step 19 deliberately allows bounded fine adjustment without changing the clock or target structure.
No fixed world seed from the report is available; default Superflat generation is used because terrain generation is not identified as part of the reproduction.
The report does not require a particular Graphics setting. Leave Graphics at the client's existing vanilla value rather than introducing an unsupported requirement.

source_meta._title: Potions, tipped arrows, and dyed leather armor render with missing or incorrect colors in the inventory

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 25w15a in a local single-player world, with the player in Creative mode and the Creative inventory's Search Items interface available.
preconditions: Use the exact affected snapshot 25w15a; do not use fix version 25w16a.
The Minecraft Launcher must be able to start Minecraft Java Edition 25w15a.
No particular world seed, coordinates, dimension, biome, structure, item possession, resource pack, graphics setting, or multiplayer server is specified by the report.
A newly created Creative-mode world is the simplest deterministic way to establish the required game mode.
If controls have been rebound, use the control assigned to the Inventory action instead of the default E key.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select or create a Java Edition installation that uses the exact snapshot version 25w15a, and launch it. Do not select 25w16a because that is listed as the fix version rather than an affected version.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft Java Edition title screen is open and identifies the running version as 25w15a.

steps.action: From the title screen, open the local-world selection menu.
steps.success_cue: The Select World screen is visible.

steps.action: Start creating a new test world. An existing world may be used instead, but creating a new one avoids unrelated inventory state.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is visible.

steps.action: Set the new world's game mode to Creative. If the game-mode control currently shows another mode, activate it until Creative is displayed.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the Game Mode control until it displays Creative
steps.success_cue: The world configuration screen explicitly shows Creative as the selected game mode.

steps.action: Create and enter the world. Leave the seed and other world-generation options at any values because the report does not require particular terrain.
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned into the world and the normal gameplay view and hotbar are visible.

steps.action: Wait before interacting until initial world loading has settled.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, the loading overlay is gone, and player input responds normally.

steps.action: Open the player inventory. Because the player is in Creative mode, this opens the Creative inventory rather than the Survival inventory interface.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open and its category tabs and item grid are visible.

steps.action: Select the Creative inventory tab labeled Search Items. If tab labels are hidden, move the pointer over the tabs until the Search Items tooltip identifies the correct one, then select it.
steps.success_cue: The Search Items tab is selected and a text search field is visible above the item grid.

steps.action: Focus the search field and remove any text that may already be present so the query will contain only the report's specified word.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the search field, press Ctrl+A, then press Backspace
steps.success_cue: The insertion cursor is active in an empty Creative inventory search field.

steps.action: Enter the report's exact search term in lowercase. No Enter key is needed; allow the item grid to refresh after the final character is typed. Do not close the inventory or take an item before handing off.
steps.success_cue: The search field contains exactly “potion”, the Creative inventory remains open, and the filtered item grid has finished populating.

stor.handoff_condition: The player is in Creative mode in Minecraft Java Edition 25w15a, the Creative inventory is open on the Search Items tab, and the exact query “potion” has just populated the filtered item grid. Hand control to the observation subsystem before changing the query, selecting an item, reloading resources, or closing the inventory.
uncertainties: The formal Steps to Reproduce directly exercise potion icons only. Although the title and comments also identify tipped arrows and dyed leather armor, the report does not provide separate acquisition, dyeing, or inventory procedures for those item classes, so they are not added as unsupported mandatory steps.

Comments mention resource reloading with F3+T, restarting the game, hotbar ordering, and color inheritance among item categories, but none of those actions is required by the report's formal reproduction steps and they are therefore omitted.

The report does not specify whether to use a new or existing world. A new Creative-mode single-player world is selected as the simplest practical way to establish the stated Creative-mode precondition.

source_meta._title: Entity models in the inventory can render outside the boundaries of the black box

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.8.8, preferably an unmodified single-player Creative-mode world with commands/cheats available, using a keyboard and mouse. The deterministic non-player entity variant described by the report is used because the report's elytra-based player variant cannot be performed in this first listed affected version.
preconditions: Launch the exact affected version Minecraft 1.8.8 rather than the fixed version 23w31a.
Use a single-player world in Creative mode with commands available.
Stand on open, solid terrain with at least several blocks of unobstructed space in front of the player so a horse can spawn and be approached.
Keep the game window large enough that the complete horse inventory interface is visible.

steps.action: Launch the Minecraft Java Edition installation configured for Minecraft 1.8.8, then verify the title screen identifies the running version as 1.8.8.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft 1.8.8 title screen is displayed.

steps.action: Create or load a single-player Creative-mode world in which commands are enabled. After entering the world, wait until nearby terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a responsive Creative-mode world and can execute commands.

steps.action: Move to a flat, unobstructed location and face toward an empty area at least two blocks away.
steps.exact_input: W/A/S/D and mouse movement as needed
steps.success_cue: There is solid, open ground approximately two blocks in front of the player with enough room for a horse.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the following legacy-version command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter: /summon EntityHorse ~ ~ ~2 {Tame:1}. This uses the historical EntityHorse identifier and Tame tag rather than modern horse command syntax. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Talk%3AHorse/Archive_1?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: A living horse is visible approximately two blocks in front of the player and no command-syntax error is shown.

steps.action: Approach the summoned horse until it is within interaction range. If the selected hotbar slot contains an item, select an empty hotbar slot before interacting so the held item does not perform another action.
steps.exact_input: W, then a number key for an empty hotbar slot if needed
steps.success_cue: The crosshair can be placed directly on the horse and the player's active hand is empty.

steps.action: Place the crosshair on the horse, hold the Sneak control—Left Shift by default—and right-click the horse once to open its inventory. If controls have been rebound, use the configured Sneak and Use/Interact controls instead. Horse inventory access while standing beside the horse uses sneak plus right-click. ([de.minecraft.wiki](https://de.minecraft.wiki/w/Inventar?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Hold Left Shift and right-click the horse once
steps.success_cue: The horse inventory interface is open, with the horse model preview visible in its dark preview area and the player's inventory slots visible below.

steps.action: Without clicking or closing the horse inventory, move the mouse cursor around the interface so the horse preview rotates through multiple orientations. Sweep the cursor near the left, right, upper, and lower edges and corners of the game window rather than leaving it stationary in the center.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse cursor around the open horse inventory interface
steps.success_cue: The horse inventory remains open and the horse preview has been rotated through several substantially different orientations; stop input and hand off immediately.

stor.handoff_condition: The horse inventory is still open in Minecraft 1.8.8, and the mouse has just been swept around the interface to rotate the horse model through multiple orientations. Begin visual observation of the inventory GUI without closing it or moving the cursor further.
uncertainties: The report's formal player-model steps require elytra, but elytra was introduced in Java Edition snapshot 15w41a and therefore is unavailable in the first listed affected version, Minecraft 1.8.8. The plan consequently uses the non-player horse-inventory variant explicitly identified in the report description. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki%3AProjects/Indonesian_translation/Alat?utm_source=openai))

The horse summon command is a deterministic setup choice not supplied by the report. Its legacy EntityHorse identifier and Tame:1 syntax were externally verified for the relevant historical command format. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Talk%3AHorse/Archive_1?utm_source=openai))

The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, GUI scale, window resolution, graphics setting, resource pack, exact horse orientation, or exact cursor coordinate. No unreported fixed value is imposed; the cursor is swept broadly to exercise the report's mouse-movement instruction.

The affected-version list contains Minecraft 1.8.8 even though the formal elytra route cannot be used there. This plan preserves Minecraft 1.8.8 as recommended_version because it is the first affected version listed, as required.
